source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design - English - Grade 9
source.notes: KICD's own Google Drive index (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ehe01q4q8G-ft1PsA0r7skcz6grZfiNQ/preview, confirmed via WebFetch) shows the official filename as 'English Grade 9 - Revised Oct.pdf', but that Drive file is download-blocked so its text could not be read directly. The document actually read here (via WebFetch's saved-local-copy + Read, full text read verbatim, NOT summarized) is cbcelimu.com's mirror, filenamed 'English-Grade-9-Formatted-April-2024.pdf' -- an earlier-dated KICD document. Its title page reads 'KENYA INSTITUTE OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT / JUNIOR SCHOOL CURRICULUM DESIGN / ENGLISH / GRADE 9', 'First published in 2024', ISBN 978-9914-43-443-9, and carries a 'DRAFT' watermark; the acknowledgement page explicitly states 'The revised Grade 9 curriculum designs were developed with the support of the World Bank through KPEELP', so this is authentically a KICD-produced document in the same revision lineage, but its exact byte-for-byte identity with the final 'Revised Oct' Drive file could not be independently confirmed. Strand/sub-strand structure, specific learning outcomes and key inquiry questions below were transcribed verbatim from this PDF's text (read directly via the Read tool, not AI-summarized), including the 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUBSTRANDS' table on p.xii-xv which was cross-checked against the full per-theme breakdown (p.1-143) for consistency -- both matched exactly. Because the exact 'Revised Oct' filename match to KICD's Drive listing could not be verified (Drive download blocked), confidence is marked 'medium' rather than 'high'; strand-level structure is very unlikely to have changed between an April/proofing pass and the October revision (KICD's rationalisation process typically only affects wording/proofing at that stage), but this has not been independently confirmed and should be spot-checked against the final Revised Oct PDF if it becomes accessible later. The app's current strand names ('Listening & Speaking', 'Reading', 'Writing', 'Grammar in Use') match the real design's 4 strands correctly -- confirmed, not previously verified against source. Grade 9 English also designates a class reader (a play) studied across all 15 themes as part of the Reading strand -- see notes on individual Reading sub-strands below.

subStrands.name: Polite Language (Euphemism)
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline words and phrases used to express euphemism
Use euphemism to show politeness in communication

Acknowledge the importance of politeness in communication
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we use polite language?
Why is it embarrassing to say some words in public?
How can we show good citizenship with regards to road safety?

subStrands.name: The Writing Process
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline the different stages of the writing process
Apply the writing process in creating a dialogue on a relevant theme
Emphasise the importance of each of the stages in the writing process in crafting flawless dialogues
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you plan your writing?
Why is it important to learn dialogue writing?
subStrands.notes: Theme 12: Personal Grooming. Second occurrence of 'The Writing Process' sub-strand, applied here specifically to dialogue writing (distinct from Theme 7's composition/story/poem focus).

subStrands.name: Creative Writing: Idioms
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the meaning of given idioms in different contexts
Use a variety of idioms in writing narrative compositions
Encourage peers to use idioms appropriately in speech and writing
keyInquiryQuestions: What are idioms?
Which idioms are you familiar with?
subStrands.notes: Theme 13: Sea Travel. Specifies 8 target idioms: peace of mind, bury the hatchet, sit on the fence, with open arms, burning bridges, follow in someone's footsteps, monkey business, adding insult to injury.

subStrands.name: Descriptive Writing
specificLearningOutcomes: Use the correct writing process to write a composition
Spell words correctly in composition writing
Apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions
Display creativity and imagination in composition writing
Recognise the importance of creativity in writing
keyInquiryQuestions: What makes a story creative?
Which words do we use to describe our different senses?
subStrands.notes: Theme 14: Sports - World Cup (Football). Design specifies target composition length of 280-320 words.

subStrands.name: Emails
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the key elements of an email
Apply the elements in writing an email
Appreciate the importance of writing emails
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we write emails?
What is the difference between emails and letters?
